what: Result of the pre-registered cloud-signature separability test. Pre-registration: cloud_prereg.json, committed at 927c4e2 with no result attached.
instrument: Siril bg / nstars / fwhm, captured per frame by the frame-QA stage into qa_work/frameqa/records.jsonl. In-house part: the block statistic only. REPORTS ONLY — no cull built, nothing gated, no deliverable touched.
statistic: Z = (median in-block - median out-of-block) / (1.4826 * MAD out-of-block)

POSITIVE_CONTROL.block: the 44 exact frame numbers in recipe.json stack.exclude (7694-7738)

NEGATIVE_CONTROL.why_this_set: zero excludes, same night as set-03 — controls pedestal, sky brightness and moon. Chosen by surveying recipe.json excludes across all 13 sets carrying frame-QA records.
NEGATIVE_CONTROL.method: every contiguous 44-frame window scanned at every start index
NEGATIVE_CONTROL.verdict_against_pre_registered_bar: DOES NOT FIRE. Bar was |Z_bg| < 5; measured worst 1.80.

HEADLINE: SEPARABLE. The cloud block reads Z_bg +6.07 where a clean set on the same night never exceeds +1.12 in the signature's own direction — a 5.4x margin. Both pre-registered bars are met.

PM_CLAIM_B.claim: nstars carries the signature MORE strongly than bg, contradicting the item's note that star count is measured blind on rich fields.
PM_CLAIM_B.verdict: SUPPORTED on this data. The star count fell 245 (8.7 MAD) while star SHAPE moved only 1.75 MAD — the frames did not get softer, so the loss is transparency rather than seeing or focus.
PM_CLAIM_B.consequence: BACKLOG:`intake-culling`'s cloud row states star COUNT is 'measured blind on rich fields (detection saturates at the cap)'. On this data it is not blind; it is the STRONGER of the two recorded signals.

PEDESTAL_TREATMENT.primary: delta bg = +1.800 ADU, absolute and denominator-free
PEDESTAL_TREATMENT.fraction_of_sky_term: +6.69 % (denominator 26.9 ADU, using pedestal 1024 which is ASSUMED and NOT measured here)
PEDESTAL_TREATMENT.why_stated: the two denominators differ by ~39x. A reader takes whichever is printed, so both are printed with their denominators and the assumed one is labelled.

LIMITS_THAT_TRAVEL_WITH_THIS_RESULT.one_set_one_night: a single positive control. This shows the recorded fields separate THIS block on THIS night; it does not establish a rate, a threshold, or generality.
LIMITS_THAT_TRAVEL_WITH_THIS_RESULT.CIRCULARITY_NOT_CLOSED_AND_THIS_IS_THE_M: how the 44 frames were selected is UNDOCUMENTED — no record in the tree states the criterion. If the operator culled by looking at bg or nstars, this test partly measures that the culler could see what they culled on.
LIMITS_THAT_TRAVEL_WITH_THIS_RESULT.partial_discriminator_run: one frame inside the block's index span (455-499) was KEPT: frame 7737, bg 1052.2, nstars 1746, fwhm 2.49. Its bg is ELEVATED (block median 1052.7, clean median 1050.9), so a simple bg threshold would have culled it and did not. That is mild evidence the cull was NOT a bg threshold, which weakly protects the bg result.
LIMITS_THAT_TRAVEL_WITH_THIS_RESULT.and_it_cuts_AGAINST_the_more_flattering_: frame 7737's nstars (1746) sits between the block (1607) and clean (1852), i.e. near where an nstars criterion would cut. So the cull is MORE consistent with an nstars-like or visual criterion than a bg one — which makes the nstars finding (the stronger, more interesting result) the half MORE exposed to circularity, not less.
LIMITS_THAT_TRAVEL_WITH_THIS_RESULT.what_would_close_it: a second cloud block on a different night whose cull criterion is recorded, or a block identified by an instrument independent of bg and nstars.

NOT_DONE_DELIBERATELY: no threshold is proposed, no cull is built, no detector is wired. The question asked was separability and only that is answered.
